$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Event Grid. See aws/s3.json for the contract. 'nano' = Nano/dev_server (core/azure_arm_core.py + core/azure_eventgrid_core.py + core/azure_locks_core.py); 'offline' = the appliance (providers/azure_services.py), which shares the SAME core/azure_eventgrid_core.py engine (event subscriptions, publish/delivery) over its own ARM state, so every level below is identical on both substrates.

azure.eventgrid.topics.crud.title: Topics — create, list, get, update, delete (generic ARM catalog)

azure.eventgrid.topics.listactions.title: "Open query" (Azure Resource Graph Explorer) and "Assign tags" on the Topics list
limitations: "Open query" runs a real Azure Resource Graph query (Microsoft.ResourceGraph/resources) over the ARM engine's own resource store: table Resources/ResourceContainers with where/project/limit/order by/count - not a canned response, but not full Kusto either (no joins, summarize or time-series operators; unsupported operators are a 400). "Assign tags" PATCHes real ARM tags onto every selected topic.

azure.eventgrid.topics.bulktags.title: "Assign tags" bulk action on the Topics list

azure.eventgrid.topic.listactions.title: Toolbar actions of a topic's Activity log and Locks panels: Export Activity Logs, Insights, Pin current filters and the Locks Subscription/Resource group scope buttons (real or local); Feedback (not simulated)
limitations: Export Activity Logs is a real subscription-scope Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings: new Administrative events are delivered to the chosen Log Analytics workspace (AzureDiagnostics) and/or storage account (container insights-activity-logs). Event Hub destinations are not served (no Event Hubs receiver). Only the Administrative category has an event source in Vyomi; Security/Policy/Alert/etc. can be enabled but never receive events. The Locks Subscription/Resource group buttons list the real Microsoft.Authorization/locks at that scope.

Insights shows counts computed from the loaded events (not the Microsoft-authored workbook); Pin current filters is a per-browser preference (it does not write a Microsoft.Portal/dashboards resource); Feedback posts to a Microsoft endpoint outside the simulator and is not simulated.

azure.eventgrid.eventsubscriptions.crud.title: Event subscriptions on a topic — create, list, get, update, delete (destination, filters)
limitations: providers/azure_services.py routes the Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions extension-resource reentry to the SAME core/azure_eventgrid_core.py engine Nano uses, over its own ARM state — the appliance is no longer behind Nano here.

azure.eventgrid.eventsubscriptions.deliv.title: Dead-lettering and retry policy (max delivery attempts, event TTL, expiration time)
limitations: Expiration time IS enforced: an event subscription past its expirationTimeUtc is swept (auto-deleted, same as real Event Grid) before any GET/list sees it. deadLetterDestination is honored to decide dead-lettered vs dropped on a failed delivery (azure.eventgrid.eventsubscriptions.delivery). maxDeliveryAttempts and eventTimeToLiveInMinutes round-trip (PUT/GET) but are not enforced as a literal attempt count / TTL countdown — there is no background retry scheduler to count attempts against (same simplification as EventBridge Scheduler's lazy firing), so a failed delivery resolves to its terminal outcome immediately rather than after N retries over the configured window.

azure.eventgrid.eventsubscriptions.deliv.title: Event delivery (filter matching, pushing to the destination endpoint, retries, dead-lettering)
limitations: REAL on publish (core/azure_eventgrid_core.py publish()/deliver(), POST {topic.properties.endpoint}): every live event subscription's filter (subjectBeginsWith/EndsWith + case sensitivity, includedEventTypes, a bounded subset of advancedFilters operators) is actually evaluated against the event, and a ServiceBusQueue/ServiceBusTopic destination is actually delivered to — the message lands in that Service Bus entity's real backlog (core/azure_servicebus_core.py), readable back over its own native wire.

StorageQueue destinations are REAL (the event JSON lands in the named queue of this environment's Storage Queue store; the queue must exist) on both substrates, and WebHook destinations are REAL offline for loopback / private-network endpoints only (no internet egress, no webhook validation handshake); on Nano there is no outbound hop, so WebHook delivery fails like an unreachable endpoint. EventHub, HybridConnection, AzureFunction and NamespaceTopic destinations have no reachable simulator backend wired yet, so delivery to them fails exactly like an unreachable real endpoint would — never a silent fake success. There is no background retry scheduler, so a failed attempt resolves immediately to dead-lettered (deadLetterDestination configured) or dropped, instead of being retried maxDeliveryAttempts times over wall-clock minutes.

azure.eventgrid.namespaces.crud.title: Namespaces — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: The MQTT broker and client/topic-space configuration on a namespace are not modeled — only the resource itself round-trips.

azure.eventgrid.systemtopics.crud.title: System topics — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: The source resource / topic type a system topic listens to is stored as configured but no Azure-service event is ever generated or delivered.

azure.eventgrid.domains.crud.title: Domains — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: Domain topics (the per-topic children of a domain) are not modeled — only the domain resource itself round-trips.

azure.eventgrid.partnerconfigurations.cr.title: Partner configurations — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: Partner authorization approval workflows are not modeled — only the configuration resource round-trips.

azure.eventgrid.partnertopics.crud.title: Partner topics — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: Partner topic activation by the partner and event delivery from a partner are not modeled.

azure.eventgrid.partnerregistrations.cru.title: Partner registrations — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: Becoming a listed Event Grid partner is not modeled — only the registration resource round-trips.

azure.eventgrid.partnernamespaces.crud.title: Partner namespaces — create, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)
limitations: Partner namespace channels and partner destinations are not modeled — only the namespace resource round-trips.

azure.eventgrid.topic.activitylog.title: Topic activity log
limitations: A simplified, generic ARM activity feed (create/update/delete on this resource), not the real Microsoft.Insights audit trail (callers, correlation ids, full operation metadata).

azure.eventgrid.topic.iam.title: Access control (IAM) on a topic
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), but the generic ARM list is subscription-wide (not scoped to this one topic), and 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation is not modelled — Vyomi never denies a console action based on a role assignment.

azure.eventgrid.topic.locks.title: Resource locks
limitations: CanNotDelete and ReadOnly locks on the topic itself ARE enforced (a locked topic's write/delete is rejected with 409 ScopeLocked, same as real ARM). The lock does not cascade to the topic's event subscriptions, which are dispatched by a separate extension-resource module (core/azure_eventgrid_core.py) and are never blocked by a lock on their parent topic.

azure.eventgrid.topic.monitoring.title: Alerts, metrics, diagnostic settings and logs on a topic
limitations: Metrics shows REAL counters derived from actual publish/delivery activity (PublishSuccessCount, MatchedEventCount, DeliverySuccessCount, DeliveryAttemptFailCount, DeadLetteredCount, DroppedEventCount — core/azure_eventgrid_core.py, never synthetic/random data), not the generic Microsoft.Insights/metrics time-series engine: no time-grain selection, chart rendering or aggregation-type picker.

Alerts and Diagnostic settings are REAL ARM extension/scoped resources (Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts, diagnosticSettings — the same generic engine every other lens resource's Alerts/Diagnostic settings page uses, core/azure_monitor_core.py): create/list/delete round-trip and validate for real. A rule's threshold is never evaluated against the counters above (no alert ever actually fires) and a diagnostic setting's logs/metrics are never delivered to the configured workspace.
Logs (Log Analytics KQL queries over ingested data) is not modeled — a genuinely separate query engine, same gap as every other Azure service's Logs tab in this simulator.

azure.eventgrid.topic.diagnose.title: Diagnose and solve problems
limitations: Runs a fixed set of REAL checks against this topic's actual configuration and delivery counters (event subscriptions present, delivery failures without a dead-letter destination, a blocking ReadOnly lock, public network access) — not Microsoft's actual diagnostics knowledge base, ML-driven root-cause analysis or automated remediation flows.

azure.eventgrid.topic.tools.title: Tasks
limitations: Tasks (Azure DevOps/Boards work-item integration) depends on a real external product/account this simulator has no counterpart for. Diagnose and solve problems is real (azure.eventgrid.topic.diagnose) and Support + Troubleshooting is the shared support-request panel (azure.common.support).

azure.eventgrid.topic.exporttemplate.title: Export template (ARM template / Bicep / Terraform)
limitations: The ARM Template tab renders this topic's own live resource JSON (type/apiVersion/properties), the same data as Overview's JSON View, in the standard ARM deployment-template envelope — real, not a static sample. Bicep and Terraform output, and the Add to library / Deploy / Visualize template actions, are not modeled.

azure.eventgrid.resourceevents.title: Event subscriptions on a resource's own system events (storage, Key Vault, App Configuration, API Management, resource group)
limitations: Subscriptions are real Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions scoped to the resource (create/list/get/delete, event types validated against what that resource type raises, expiration swept, per-subscription matched/delivered/failed counters). A resource group's (and the subscription's) subscriptions receive REAL Microsoft.Resources.ResourceWriteSuccess/ResourceDeleteSuccess events from every actual ARM write/delete in it.

Storage, Key Vault, App Configuration and API Management do not yet emit their data-plane system events on their own (BlobCreated, SecretNewVersionCreated, KeyValueModified, …): those fire only from the console's 'Send test event' (simulateEvent) action. Delivery is real only to Service Bus queue/topic destinations on the offline appliance; WebHook, Storage Queue and Event Hub destinations (and every destination on Nano) are unreachable and resolve to dead-lettered/dropped, as for topic subscriptions.
